published_figures.source: Cessna Model 172P Pilot's Operating Handbook, 12 May 1981
published_figures.figure: Section 2, powerplant limitations: "The static RPM range at full throttle (carburetor heat off and mixture leaned to maximum RPM) is 2300 to 2420 RPM."

Section 1, performance specifications: ground roll 890 ft; figure 5-5 gives it for a short-field take-off - flaps 10, full throttle before brake release, paved level dry runway, zero wind, sea level, 2400 lb - with lift-off at 51 KIAS, which figure 5-1 makes 55.6 KCAS with 10 degrees of flap.

Section 1, performance specifications: rate of climb at sea level 700 FPM; figure 5-6 gives it at 76 KIAS, flaps up, full throttle, 2400 lb, and 700 between its 0 C and 20 C columns at the standard 15 C. 76 KIAS is 75.4 KCAS by figure 5-1.
Figure 5-8, cruise performance: 121 KTAS at 8000 ft, standard temperature, 2650 RPM (77% power), 2400 lb, mixture leaned. Section 1 gives 120 knots at 75% power at 8000 ft.

Figure 3-1, maximum glide: 65 KIAS, propeller windmilling, flaps up, zero wind, drawn as 18 nautical miles from 12,000 ft above the terrain, which is 9.1 to 1. 65 KIAS is 66 KCAS by figure 5-1. The figure is a chart, read by eye; the tolerance allows for that.
Figure 5-3, stall speeds, 2400 lb, power off, wings level, flaps up: 51 KCAS at the most rearward centre of gravity and 52 KCAS at the most forward. The range is 2 kt either side of those.
Figure 5-3, stall speeds, 2400 lb, power off, wings level, flaps 10 degrees: 48 KCAS rearward and 49 KCAS forward centre of gravity, 2 kt either side.
Figure 5-3, stall speeds, 2400 lb, power off, wings level, flaps 30 degrees: 46 KCAS at either centre of gravity, 2 kt either side.
